text: Manuals on writing emphasize the discipline of "pen to paper," or "fingers to keyboard," but attend less to the writing that happens in your head.

chapter: Chapter 18: Expressing What's In There
text: 关于写作的手册强调“笔触纸”或“手指敲键盘”的纪律，但很少关注在头脑中进行的写作。

chapter: Chapter 18: Expressing What's In There
text: Write your stuff, hide it, let it stack up. Reread it. Don't worry about it. Don't look for perfection. To switch metaphors, your first writing is as delicate as a seedling. Don't show it to some yahoo who wouldn't know an orchid from kudzu.把你的东西写出来，藏起来，让它堆积起来。重读一遍。不要担心它。不要追求完美。打个比方说吧，你的第一稿就像一株幼苗一样脆弱。不要拿给某个连兰花和葛藤都分不清的蠢货看。

chapter: Chapter 18: Expressing What's In There
text: Whether or not you identify yourself as a writer, putting thoughts, ideas, and feelings on paper is a great way to get the inside out. Because cathartic writing, or journaling, is for your eyes only, you get to release what's inside while maintaining privacy. Go ahead, scream on the paper or whisper your secrets. It's your paper. Whether you just need to vent or have a book inside you, here are some tips for getting started: 无论你是否认为自己是作家，把思想、想法和感受写在纸上，都是把内心世界表达出来的好方法。因为宣泄性写作或日记是只为你自己看的，所以你可以释放内心的感受，同时保持隐私。大胆些，在纸上尖叫或低语你的秘密。这是你的纸。无论你只是需要发泄，还是有书稿在心中，以下是一些开始写作的建议：• Write daily. Even a small chunk of time, fifteen or twenty minutes each day, gets your mind oriented to what you're putting on the paper. Just as small, frequent meals aid metabolism of food, small, frequent writing sessions aid metabolism of ideas. I tell my clients that the time between sessions is as important as the time in session. Therapy is most effective when the client has the capacity to metabolize ideas raised in the sessions, to come in hungry next time, and obtain more food for

chapter: Chapter 18: Expressing What's In There
text: thought. Writing works the same way. The best writing generates more to think about, and more to write. • 每天写作。即使是一小块时间，每天十五到二十分钟，也能让你的大脑适应你在纸上表达的内容。就像小而频繁的饮食有助于食物的代谢一样，小而频繁的写作有助于思想的代谢。我告诉我的客户，两次写作之间的休息时间与写作时间一样重要。当客户有能力代谢在治疗过程中提出的思想，并在下一次治疗时带着饥饿感到来，获得更多的思考素材时，治疗是最有效的。写作也是如此。最好的写作会产生更多的思考内容，以及更多的写作素材。• Make it easy. Have your materials ready. If you want a special "container" for your thoughts, take the time to browse the aisle of journals at your favorite bookstore. I think of a journal in the way Mr. Ollivander of the Harry Potter world regarded the right wand: it will pick you. On the other hand, some beautiful journals are left untouched because the writer is afraid to spoil it. A journal is not effective if it inhibits the writer. Sometimes a cheap notebook is a better option. Or, look in the dollar bins at a large craft or discount store. I have found some lovely journals this way, and I feel free to waste as many pages as I want. • 让一切变得简单。准备好你的材料。如果你想要一个特殊的“容器”来装你的想法，就花点时间在你喜欢的书店的日记本过道上浏览一番。我认为日记本就像哈利･波特世界

chapter: Chapter 18: Expressing What's In There
text: 里的奥利凡多先生看待合适的魔杖一样：它会挑选你。另一方面，有些漂亮的日记本因为作家害怕弄坏它而无人问津。如果日记本限制了作家，它就起不到作用。有时候，廉价的笔记本是一个更好的选择。或者，在大型手工艺品或折扣商店的美元区看看。我就是这样找到一些可爱的日记本的，而且我觉得自己可以随心所欲地浪费多少页都行。• Write crap. As Ann Lamott puts it in Bird by Bird, write "shitty first drafts." If you are writing only for yourself, the function is just to get it out: forget punctuation and grammar. Practice not editing. Write down your shopping list if that's on your mind, or write about why you don't want to write. See if you can "talk" on paper. Listen to your thoughts and record what they say. If you are writing for literary purposes, practice shitty first drafts, and go back and edit your work as many times as necessary. • 写垃圾。正如安·拉莫特在《鸟鸟》中所说，写“糟糕的初稿”。如果你只是为自己写作，功能就是把它写出来：忘记标点符号和语法。练习不编辑。写下你的购物清单，如果这是你的心事，或者写下你为什么不想写作。看看你是否能在纸上“交谈”。倾听你的思想，记录它们所说的话。如果你是为了文学目的而写作，练习糟糕的初稿，然后回去多次编辑你的作品。• Tell the truth. This is the writer's mantra. You'll feel tempted to filter and soften what's inside you. Catch yourself, and write the raw truth. As Natalie Goldberg says in her inspiring

chapter: Chapter 18: Expressing What's In There
text: manual, Wild Mind, "Writing is the crack through which you can crawl into a bigger world, into your wild mind." Take on the challenge of finding words for the truth, rather than making truth fit your words. • 说出真相。这是作家的座右铭。你会忍不住过滤和软化你内心的感受。要意识到这一点，并写下原始的真相。正如娜塔莉·戈德堡在她鼓舞人心的手册《狂野心灵》中所说：“写作是你可以爬进一个更广阔世界、进入你狂野心灵的裂缝。”接受挑战，为真相找到词语，而不是让真相符合你的词语。• Write your pain. James W. Pennebaker and his associates at the University of Texas have conducted extensive research on the benefits of journaling. His findings: if you want relief, write about your most upsetting experiences, write through the pain, and connect painful events with your life story. Getting to the tough stuff was a key factor in helping people feel better and move on. • 写下你的痛苦。詹姆斯·W·彭内巴克和他在德克萨斯州大学的同事们对写日记的好处进行了广泛的研究。他的发现：如果你想得到解脱，就写下你最令人不安的经历，通过写作来排解痛苦，并将痛苦的事件与你的生活故事联系起来。直面困难是帮助人们感觉更好、继续前进的关键因素。• Respect your writing. If it is time to write, don't wait until you have time. Make commitments to yourself, and ask others to hold you accountable. You can commit

chapter: Chapter 18: Expressing What's In There
text: to a certain amount of time each day, or to a quota. For her creativity course, Julia Cameron assigns three full "morning pages" per day and, for those wanting a literary life, See insists on one thousand words a day. Find what fits you, and fit it in. • 尊重你的写作。如果到了该写作的时候，不要等到你有空的时候再写。要对自己做出承诺，并让别人监督你。你可以每天承诺写一定的时间，或者完成一定的任务量。朱莉娅·卡梅隆在她的创意课程中要求每天写三页完整的“晨间随笔”，而西则坚持每天写一千字。找到适合你的方法，并坚持下去。• Record life. Anne Lamott emphasizes the importance of taking notes rather than trusting memory. Her advice: always carry a pen and some index cards. Jot down enough to remind you of your ideas and observations, then pull out your cards at your daily writing session and expand. • 记录生活。安妮·拉莫特强调了记笔记的重要性，而不是依赖记忆。她的建议是：随身携带一支笔和一些索引卡片。记下足够的内容来提醒你自己的想法和观察，然后在每天的写作时间里拿出卡片进行扩展。

text: 我甚至认为，以父亲卓越的智慧，他应该知道我想说什么。然而，他并不会读心术。此外，连接在这台20世纪80年代老式录音机上的麦克风也无法捕捉我内心世界的声音。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 我一定是有什么问题
text: 一切看起来好像永远都不会好转。有一次，我彻底崩溃了。一天半夜我突然醒来，一边歇斯底里地大声哭泣，一边把我个人存在的问题和生活中遇到的所有问题全部输入电脑文档中。我再也承受不了了，我太另类了，生活一团糟。这个世界人太多、太吵闹、太苛刻。最终我决定用一种原始的、不加梳理的方式把我内心积累的所有秘密情绪全部表达出来，只有这样才能拯救自己。重读自己所写的文字后，我意识到我不能一直这样生活下去。总之，我挺过了那个可怕的夜晚。不久之后，我对自我有了一些新发现，从而改变了自己的生活。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 我的使命
text: 将自己的感受真诚地表达出来，减轻了我所感受到的一些痛苦；与其他内向者建立联系，也让我不再认为自己的行为有多么“怪异”。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 为什么内向者不擅长用语言表达思想
text: 努力想找到合适的词进行表达的过程被称为“词汇提取”，这是许多内向者都存在困难的过程。在社交场合中，缺乏“词汇提取”能力，我们就很难跟上外向者敏捷的语言表达节奏。工作中，我们可能给别人留下自己不知道自己在说什么的印象，但实际上我们心里很清楚想表达的意思。课堂上，我们不敢举手回答问题，因为当同学的目光都落在我们身上时，我们很难用语言表达自己的观点。内向者存在“词汇提取”问题，其中一个原因是我们对信息处理得过于深入。对想法，我们会仔细思考，在脑海中反复思量，从各个角度分析。当大脑处于“反思模式”时，我们就很难用语言表达出来。内向者做不到像许多外向者那样边想边说，我们得在心里想好再说。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 为什么内向者不擅长用语言表达思想
text: 莱尼博士认为，内向者更喜欢长期记忆而不是工作记忆。如果事实如此，就可以解释为什么“词汇提取”对我们来说如此困难了。提取长期记忆中存储的信息相对困难。要“调出”你试图回忆的信息，需要正确的联想或“钥匙”——让你想起存储的记忆的东西。例如，如果你想回忆第一天上幼儿园的情景，那么试着环顾房间四周，看看能不能找到能调出你回忆的“钥匙”。假如你看见了一双运动鞋，这时你可能会突然想起，上幼儿园的第一天，有人把牛奶洒在了你的鞋子上，于是，那天的许多回忆便如潮水般涌入你的脑海。而且如果你在试图发言时，哪怕只有一丁点儿焦虑，比如有人让你当场发言，你可能更难找出正确的话语来表达。并非所有内向的人都生性腼腆或有社交焦虑，但内向的人在社交场合确实都会经历某种程度的焦虑。焦虑会让人感到疲惫，这时，回忆信息的难度就增加了，这是因为焦虑时大脑中会释放大量的压力荷尔蒙——皮质醇。皮质醇会影响大脑，导致记忆力减退，妨碍回忆。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 为什么内向者不擅长用语言表达思想
text: 对一个内向的人来说，表达思想的最好方法就是把想法写出来。例如，比起打电话和面对面的会议，你可能更喜欢用短信和电子邮件的形式进行沟通。同样，许多内向的人都会通过写日记的方式消化自己的各种经历。产生这种偏好的原因仍然与我们大脑的运作方式有关。莱尼博士说，人们在说话和写作时使用的大脑通路不同，对于内向的人来说，“写作”通路更顺畅。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 内向者与外向者对待冲突的不同方式
text: 内向者与外向者对待冲突的不同方式内向者对待冲突的方式与外向者不同。发生冲突时，外向者通常会选择当即处理，一通语言和情绪宣泄后，问题就解决了。而内向的人需要时间消化受到的伤害。冲突出现之初，他们往往会选择撤退而不是争吵，因为他们需要时间和空间思考所发生的事。两种处理方式虽然不同，但没有好坏之分。然而，如果伴侣不了解对方应对冲突的方式，就会出现问题。首先，在内向者—外向者型情感中，内向者可能无法接受外向者强烈而突然的发泄，就像被车灯突然照射到的小鹿，会慌乱到不知所措。为了避免更大的冲突，他们只得选择向伴侣妥协（“好吧，我和你一起去参加生日聚会！这件事就这样过去可以吗？”）。外向者无知地以为自己吵赢了，便按自己的方式行事，然而他们根本没有意识到，自己的胜利并不真实，反而在伴侣心中埋下了怨恨的种子。而内向的人只得内化自己的痛苦。他们不会再提及这件事，而是独自烦恼忧伤（我经常为此感到难过）。而他们的伴侣并不知道自己越了界，所以会重复这样的行为，最终将内向的那个人逼到崩溃（“我正为这个想法感到激动呢，你就对我指指点点，我讨厌你，你为什么要这样？！”）。这种反应让伴侣大吃一惊，因为他们不知道内向的伴侣什么时候产生了这样的想法。但对于内向者而言，痛苦一直都真实存在，可能会沉淀几天，也可能几个星期甚至几年。最后，伴侣之间可能会采取被动攻击的行为（“我没有

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 内向者与外向者对待冲突的不同方式
text: 生气，只是希望这一次你能考虑一下我的需求。”）。如我所说，这种情况往往发生在内向者—内向者型伴侣之间。因为两人都不想谈论问题，都选择忽视，都期望问题能够自动消失。然而，感情中的冲突几乎不会自动消失。相反，如果不能从根源上得到解决，问题还会反复露头。

text: 安科维茨说：“通过自我反思，注意哪些工作能够发挥你的能量，哪些工作会消耗你的能量，你就知道什么工作能让你展现最好的自己了。”

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 选择适合的职业领域
text: 可以穿着睡衣在家做的工作（没开玩笑）谋生并不一定就得干朝九晚五的工作。许多内向者走的是自由职业的道路，原因可以理解：我们喜欢创业，我们独立，我们有远大的理想。此外，如果能够自行控制自己的工作方式，我们就不会感到那么疲惫，每天都能省出一些精力与亲友互动。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 内向者需要有意义的工作
text: 他们渴望的是一份能够展示真实自我的工作——发挥他们的兴趣特长和技能，符合他们的价值观和个性。换句话说，他们想“做真实的自己”。实际上，内向者在生活中的各个领域都感觉不到完整，除非他们的外在生活能够体现他们的内心世界。如果其他人无法看到真实的他们（他们内心的秘密世界），他们就会感到生活不完整，从而对生活产生不满情绪。

text: 内心世界能激发创造力。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 内向者的内心世界
text: 内心世界的感觉和感受难以用语言描述。“有些人认为自己的思想就像一个个整齐的盒子，但我的思想更像是一片奔腾的水域，情感、记忆、思想和灵感都融为一体。”

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 从数字看内向者与创造力
text: 作为一个内向的人，我不擅长用语言表达自己的感受，所以喜欢用艺术的方式表达我的内心。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 内向者的创作过程
text: 具有创造力还有一个关键：需要放飞思想。当你思想神游、做白日梦或者思绪乱飞时，研究员们有一个专业术语形容这种状态，叫作“创意孵化”。这个词的意思是，虽然你并没有有意识地思考一个问题，但你的大脑仍然在后台工作，就像智能手机上的应用程序，虽然你没有使用，但程序仍在运行。有时，当你洗碗或洗澡时，脑海中突然就会冒出一个想法——“啊哈！”就像电灯泡突然亮起来一样。

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 过度思考的折磨
text: 有时，你的想象简直就是天马行空。前一刻你还想象着开心的事，比如和伴侣一起悠闲地散步，下一秒，一个黑暗的想法可能就会涌入你的脑海。吉尔说，她过度思考时，通常都是从小事开始，然后一发不可收拾，最终完全失控。“前一分钟我还在感受一首歌的美好寓意，下一秒脑海中的场景就变成我在商场与恐怖分子搏斗后英勇牺牲，开始制作自己葬礼上用的幻灯片。”

book: I型人格：一本书全方位解析MBTI中的内倾型人格
chapter: 过度思考的感觉
text: 过度思考的感觉每个人（包括外向的人）都会有过度思考的时候，但内向的人过度思考的频率更高。几个内向的人告诉我，过度思考对他们来说就是第二天性，有时他们甚至意识不到自己在过度思考。我问内向者：“如果你意识到自己正在过度思考，你会有什么感觉？”他们说：过度思考时，就好像同时打开了无数个水龙头。——蒂娜当你不得不与一个人进行一场艰难的谈话，就算你在脑海中已经想象过成千上万种对话方式，你还是要面对现实，这感觉就像一记耳光把你打回现实。——蒂芙尼(Tiffany)过度思考的感觉就像一个黑洞，让我越陷越深。哪怕是一道选择题，我都会联想到无数结果或可能性。我总是担心自己做出的选择会对他人造成怎样的影响，或者对十年后有什么影响。——朱莉(Julie)过度思考时，我感觉自己就像身处迷雾之中，有时甚至会大声说出脑海中臆想的事。即使只有我一个人，也很尴尬。——妮科尔过度思考时，我总感觉自己丧失了能力，无法做出决定。我适应能力强，做事讲策略，所以总是会考虑所有可能发生的情况，结果考虑过度，竟无从决定了。这让我的焦虑油然而生。我不光是在做决策时会过度思考，有时还会对人们说的话过度思考，因而导致焦虑。但实际上，他们的话并没有任何弦外之意。——希拉里(Hillary)我感觉，过度思考就像大脑处于一个繁忙的十字路口，红绿灯任意闪烁，大量信息任意穿梭，没有任何方向感。——罗伯特

chapter: 发病契机与发病原因并不相同
text: 近期的丧失、被抛弃的体验唤醒年幼时的痛苦记忆并引发病症的情况，在边缘型人格障碍案例中占据压倒性比重。

chapter: 第二章 边缘型人格障碍的症状
text: 边缘型人格障碍的诸多症状中，最为主要的便是情绪波动激烈。患者会短时间内在情绪、人际关系、行为举止、自我认同等方面出现巨大的态度变化，前后判若两人。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 对被抛弃的强烈恐惧边缘型人格障碍患者非常惧怕被抛弃。这种恐惧始自双方关系拉近的瞬间，随着亲密程度和对对方的依赖程度增加而增加。无论是朋友、恋人、家人、主治医生、咨询师或协助人员，当对方成为对患者而言重要的存在，患者的恐惧便会加深。只要对方态度稍一冷淡，或者一些行为使患者感到自己被厌弃，便会触发患者的不安。患者往往会基于对方细微的行为或态度得出对方感到自己是麻烦、准备抛弃自己的极端结论，进而感到自己毫无价值。为了避免被抛弃，患者会近乎疯狂地努力抓住对方。然而，刻意讨好或拖延时间，有时反而会让对方感到烦躁。如若对方态度更加冷漠或进行威压，患者便会越发地感到被抛弃，从而恐惧更甚，忽生怒意，攻击对方，或在冲动下采取危险行为。这也是患者面临严重的人际关系问题的重要原因之一。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 人际关系不稳定，反复于极端之间边缘型人格障碍的特征之一，是人际关系变动激烈。患者起初会理想化地看待关系，在发生使其失望或违背预期的事情后，便会感觉自己遭到背叛，一切都那么难以忍受。即便是一些小小的要求得不到满足，也会破口大骂，开始全方位地贬低对方，对于对方的评价前后迥然。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 有情感饥渴问题的人，对倾注于自身的情感和关注受到极细小的威胁也十分敏感。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 任何人处于缺乏关爱的环境中时，都会产生不信任、自我否定及愤怒等情感。与此相对，如果处于获得关注、自身价值能够得到认同的环境中，人便能充满活力地以爱和奉献回馈周围的人。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 事实上，很多时候，问题仅在于患者的生活环境，只要将患者置于使其安心、能够获得认同的环境中，其症状不仅能够得到改善，其本人还能展现出极具魅力的人格。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 患者周围的人往往因其前后判若两人而惊诧。然而，在怒火的驱使下，患者经常会忘却所有，不顾场合和状况，做出过激反应。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 一般情况下，在出现自杀意图或自残行为后，患者会在一段时间内状态安稳。究其原因，是患者通过上述行为实现自我净化，释放了内心压力，并且感受到周围人的关爱，其情感饥渴的状态暂时得到满足。

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 暴饮暴食和偷窃，常常是为了治愈情感饥渴的替代行为。对于哺乳期的幼儿而言，“吃”不单是进食行为，还是感受关爱的行为。赠予、购买行为，在很大程度上起到代替此类直接获得关爱行为的作用

chapter: 边缘型人格障碍的诊断方法
text: 长久的空虚感边缘型人格障碍患者，常常感到一种慢性空虚。即便在诸事顺利的情况下，患者也容易为模糊的空虚感所环绕。明明应当感到幸福时，患者也易隐隐地感到不满。还有人不习惯幸福的状态，处于幸福的状态时反而感到不适。在事情发展不顺利时，患者的空虚感则会更强。在患者的心中，之前的努力、积蓄，以及珍视的所有会因细碎龃龉或不满而丧失一切意义。患者甚至会自暴自弃，认为连生命本身也毫无意义。要摆脱空虚感的折磨，就需要刺激。正因为此，边缘型人格障碍的患者容易沉湎于追求危险刺激的行为。浪费和暴饮暴食，也容易成为消解慢性空虚的行为。

chapter: 自我与他人的边界模糊
text: 自我与他人的边界模糊随着研究深入，边缘型人格障碍的另一认知特性也逐渐清晰——患者不能明确区分自我与客体，模糊两者边界，容易混淆自我的视角与他人的视角。比如，患者认为自己喜爱的事物，他人也必定喜爱；反之，自己厌恶的事物，他人也必定厌恶。即便是在大脑中清楚自我与客体是两个不同的存在，自我与他人的感受也不同，却会在不知不觉中混淆两者。

chapter: 自我与他人的边界模糊
text: 美国精神医学专家奥托·科恩伯格(Otto F. Kernberg)根据客体关系的成熟度，将人格组织分为以下三类。①精神病性人格组织。自我与客体区分混乱，自我边界模糊。②边缘性人格组织。在一定程度上维持自我与客体的区分，在承受压力时或处于不成体系的状况中时，自我与客体的区分模糊，容易产生混乱。③神经症性人格组织。虽然自我与客体区分明晰，由于压抑的内心矛盾，易在与客体的关系中发生不安与紧张状态。

chapter: 自我与他人的边界模糊
text: 患者也容易被卷入他人的情绪之中。患者不仅容易被他人的情绪感染，还倾向于认为自身情绪会影响他人

chapter: 缺乏安全感
text: 缺乏安全感患者的自我与客体边界模糊，容易混淆自我与他人，这意味着有时患者容易受到他人影响，感到自我同一性始终受到外界威胁。虽然人在承受巨大压力时都会出现这种状态，但是这对边缘型人格障碍患者而言却是家常便饭。因此，边缘型人格障碍患者缺乏基本的安全感和归属感。

chapter: 好奇心旺盛，容易厌倦
text: 好奇心旺盛，容易厌倦与情绪管理问题相关的特征，是患者好奇心旺盛，而旺盛的好奇心又影响着患者的行为模式。好奇心旺盛，既有容易分神、厌倦的一面，又有富有感性、创造性和自我表现力的一面。在诗人、作家、音乐家、演员等艺术家中存在较多边缘型人格障碍患者的情况，也许与此特性有关。一般认为，求新求奇的心态与药物滥用存在较强关联。人的好奇心很大程度上受到秉性影响。因此与其称好奇为一种性格，不如认为是一种气质。虽然不是所有边缘型人格障碍患者都表现出强烈的好奇心，但是典型的患者一般都具备此特性。典型患者中，也有在童年时期出现注意缺陷与多动障碍(ADHD)倾向的患者。曾经遭受虐待的患者，很容易出现多动障碍倾向。

chapter: 好奇心旺盛，容易厌倦
text: 他既渴求家人的关爱，却又必须保持距离，这深层原因必然是他曾经受伤、不能安稳的心。

chapter: 思维极端化
text: 从认知的角度来看，边缘型人格障碍的根本问题之一在于患者容易陷入极端化思维。非黑即白，非满即无，非成功即失败，非友即敌——患者的观点两极化，没有中间地带。“一件事不顺利，我就觉得事事不顺。然后厌倦一切，想放弃一切。”

chapter: 思维极端化
text: “失败了，就没办法再退后了。争吵之后，怎么可能和好呢。如果在关系中受挫，我就会想逃避，不再见面，什么都不看。”

chapter: 发自内心地否定自我
text: 她面容稚嫩，但是与其说天真无邪，不如说有一种不得父母关爱的人身上特有的、虚长年华的幼稚感和阴郁感。

chapter: 对父母的强烈执念
text: 所有患者都存在过度理想化父母，然后感到失望的情况。

chapter: 萎缩的自恋
text: 自恋型人格障碍患者具备压制双亲影像的强势夸大自体，极少为双亲影像所击溃。边缘型人格障碍患者面临强大的双亲影像，其夸大自体则十分羸弱。即便是希望鼓起夸大自体以对抗双亲影像，也无能为力。

chapter: “真实的自我”抗拒“虚假的自我”
text: 边缘型人格障碍的基本障碍，包括整合功能和自我功能脆弱、情绪管理不力、一分为二且自我否定的认知模式。

chapter: “真实的自我”抗拒“虚假的自我”
text: 在这些障碍背后，是患者源自被抛弃的过往体验的情感饥渴、与双亲的隔阂、曾遭受创伤且不稳定的自恋问题。

chapter: 1 从亲子关系分析
text: 边缘型人格障碍患者中感觉遭到父亲拒绝的人所占比例高于感觉遭到母亲拒绝的人。边缘型人格障碍的背景中，常常能看到患者父亲的缺位或被拒绝。

chapter: 4 回避性类型——对受伤过于敏感
text: 如果承认自己对某人的爱恋，倘若遭到拒绝或失去对方时，自己便会受伤。患者对这种情况感到恐惧，因此便选择事先设好防线——对他人、对自己隐藏心意。

chapter: 泰然处之，使其安心
text: 感到孤立无援，是使患者出现极端行为的重要原因。

chapter: 找出不良行为模式
text: 在记录表格上书写对负面事件的反应和情绪的方法，有助于患者整理思绪、积累经验。边缘型人格障碍患者具备活在此时此刻的倾向，而话语会助长这一倾向。在患者独白的精神分析中，或在与患者的对话心理治疗中，我们都很难控制患者思维容易扩散的倾向。患者的自由讲述容易为感情洪流所驱使，失去方向。书写则能够很好地弥补整合功能弱的问题。按照一定样式书写、整理，可使患者避免迷失方向，直面重要问题。

chapter: 找出不良行为模式
text: 当患者具备一定程度回顾自身的能力时，我们也可采用对话方式实施治疗。但是在患者思维仍然混乱时，采用书写方式的治疗往往更为顺畅。

chapter: 书写和对话的功效
text: 书写和对话的功效书写和对话，对边缘型人格障碍的改善具有重要作用。书写有利于提升大脑前额叶皮质功能。在持续书写的过程中，人对情绪和行为的控制也会好转。在保持恰到好处的距离的前提下，与某一能够信任的对象通过邮件或信息沟通，也能成为患者的精神支柱。

chapter: 书写和对话的功效
text: 对于黑塞而言，撰写书信不仅是倾倒不满与烦恼、整理情绪的工具，还是寻求面对困难时的解决方法、明确自身需求的方法——即“寻求自身手段”。书信，也是黑塞作为作家的修行。黑塞试图通过表达其过敏神经承担的来自外界的种种压力，以克服一切障碍。黑塞在书信及日记中书写自己遭遇的种种不快。他不仅描述状况，也讲述心境。这一过程有利于黑塞客观看待状况、缓和不快，也对黑塞寻找到真实自我大有裨益。正如认知疗法认为各种问题都是促使自身成长的绝佳动力，黑塞每日经历的问题和不快经历都是他撰写书信时的材料。日后遭遇的试炼和苦恼，也成为黑塞小说的素材和动力。此时，黑塞看待事物的观点因此发生了骤变。持续书写对话，能够使人认识到即便是问题也有积极一面，进入一分为二的认知方式。

chapter: 整合自身
text: 整合自身边缘型人格障碍康复道路上最为关键的阶段，是患者回顾到目前为止的人生、将自身经历及其意义整合为一个故事。在书写和讲述的过程中，患者逐步厘清自己备受煎熬、走投无路的过程，理解围绕自己的家族史整体。随着重新整合自身，患者会逐渐摆脱过往创伤及束缚，重新夺回对自身主体性的控制权。

chapter: 好的自我，坏的自我，真正的自我
text: 克服边缘型人格障碍核心病理的过程，是整合分裂的自我的过程。这既是一个极为辩证的过程，也是一个不止步于克服二元论的认知方式、与确立自我有关的问题。

chapter: 5. Forgetting to Remember the Future
text: Underdevelopment best explains another time-related malfunction of the ADD brain, the chronic incapacity to consider the future. e guiding assumption of the adult with attention deﬁcit disorder, like that of the small child, seems to be that only the present exists and needs to be taken into account. He lives as if his actions had no implications for the future,no eﬀects on future needs, relationships or responsibilities. e short-term goal is invariably chosen over the long-term, with the exception of activities or projects capable of arousing the sluggish motivation-reward nexus in the brain. e present impulse dominates. It has been aptly said that people with ADD forget to remember the future. In the moment of action or decision making, ADD adults are no more mindful of consequences than a young child. 发育不良最好地解释了ADD大脑的另一个与时间相关的故障，即慢性无法考虑未来。对于患有注意力缺陷障碍的成年人来说，与年幼的孩子一样，似乎只有现在存在，并且需要加以考虑。他生活得好像他的行为对未来没有任何影响，对未来的需求、关系或责任没有任何影响。短期目标总是优先于长期目标，除非活动或项目能够激发大脑中迟钝的动机-奖励联系。现在冲动占主导地位。有人恰如其分地说，患有ADD的人忘记记住未来。在行动或决策时，ADD成年人对后果的意识并不比年幼的孩子强。

chapter: 6. Different Worlds: Heredity and the Environments of Childhood
text: ADD is also found more commonly in people whose ﬁrst-degree relatives are alcoholics or suﬀer from depression, anxiety, addiction, obsessive-compulsive disorder or Tourette’s syndrome. It may appear from such facts that this motley collection of related syndromes is largely hereditary—but to assume that would be like believing that if there are three generations of butchers or bakers or candlestick makers in a family, then meat cutting,baking and candle manufacturing must also be genetic. e family atmosphere in which the child spends the early formative years has a major impact on brain development. It is obvious that brain/mind problems such as ADD are far more likely to develop in families where the parents are struggling with dysfunction or psychological problems of their own. It would be astonishing if children growing up in such unsettled environments did not develop some of the same problems. chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: In the language of psychology, mental absence, tuning out, is an example of a mind state known as dissociation.1 It is employed in clinical psychiatry to refer to speciﬁc syndromes such as multiple personalitydisorder, but I use the term in its general sense. Dissociation, including the tuning-out of ADD, originates in a defensive need—it is a form of psychological defense. Gloucester’s motive to be “distract,” in the fourth act of King Lear, is very close to the source of the “distractness” of ADD. It is a way of coping with emotional hurt. e original purpose of dissociation is to separate conscious awareness from some emotional pain we areexperiencing, to dis-associate one from the other. We may think of dissociation as a psychological anesthetic. 从心理学的角度讲，心不在焉、神思恍惚是一种分离性失神发作。1在临床精神病学中，它被用来指代多重人格障碍等特定综合征，但我在此使用这个术语的一般意义。分离性失神发作，包括注意力缺陷多动障碍的心不在焉症状，起源于一种防御性需求，是一种心理防御机制。在《李尔王》第四幕中，格洛斯特想要“心烦意乱”的动机，与注意力缺陷多动障碍的“心烦意乱”症状的根源非常接近。这是一种应对情感伤害的方式。分离性失神发作的原始目的是将我们的意识知觉与我们正在经历的一些情感痛苦分离，使两者互不关联。我们可以将分离性失神发作视为一种心理麻醉剂。

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: Episodic experiences of a distressing nature do not inducedissociation, but chronic distress does—the distress of the sensitive infant with unsatisﬁed attunement needs, for example. e infant has to dissociate chronic emotional pain from consciousness for two reasons.First, it is too overwhelming for his fragile nervous system. He simply cannot exist in what we might call a state of chronic negative arousal, with adrenaline and other stress hormones pumping through his veins all the time. It is physiologically too toxic. He has to block it out. Second, if the parent’s anxiety is the source of the infant’s distress, the infant unconsciously senses that fully expressing his own emotional turmoil will only heighten that anxiety. His distress would then be aggravated—a vicious cycle he can escape by tuning out.

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: 令人痛苦的经历不会引起“分离”，但长期的痛苦会——例如，敏感的婴儿在得不到情感上的满足时所感到的痛苦。婴儿必须将慢性情感痛苦从意识中分离出来有两个原因。首先，对于他脆弱的神经系统来说，这种痛苦太强烈了。他不能一直处于我们所说的慢性负面唤起状态，肾上腺素和其他应激激素会一直冲击他的静脉。生理上来说，这太有毒了。他必须将其排除在外。第二，如果父母的焦虑是婴儿痛苦的原因，婴儿会无意识地感觉到，充分表达自己的情绪波动只会加剧这种焦虑。他的痛苦就会加重——他可以通过不听来逃脱这种恶性循环。

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: e survival value of all psychological defenses is relatively short-lived. 所有心理防御的生存价值都是相对短暂的。

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: Sooner or later dissociation becomes a hindrance, interferes with life and slows psychological growth. e tuned-out individual has diﬃculty learning from experience and is hampered in making contact with others.e inner retreat from psychological reality means that he may never learn to cope with emotional setbacks in a creative and positive way. We may compare any psychological defense to a heavy fur coat a man in a cold northern climate puts on to keep from freezing. Wearing the fur coat saves his life. Let’s imagine that he is suddenly transported to the equator, coat still on. He would soon ﬁnd that the clothing that helped him survive in the north makes him most uncomfortable or even ill in his new circumstances. Of course, our traveler is free to remove his coat. e problem with unconscious psychological defenses is that they cannot be shed at will. ey were induced without our conscious will in the ﬁrstplace, indeed before we had any will at all. 分离迟早会成为一种障碍，干扰生活，减缓心理成长。自我封闭的人难以从经验中学习，在与他人交往方面受到阻碍。从心理上远离现实意味着，他可能永远无法学会以一种创造性和积极的方式应对情感挫折。我们可以把任何一种心理防御机制比作一个人在寒冷的北方穿上厚厚的皮大衣以避免冻僵。穿上皮大衣救了他的命。让我们想象一下，他突然被转移到赤道，皮大衣还穿在身上。他很快就会发现，在北方帮助他生存下来的衣服，在新环境中让他感到最不舒服，甚至生病。当然，我们的旅行者可以自由地脱下他的外套。无意识心理防御的问题在

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: 于，它们不能随意摆脱。它们首先是在我们没有意识的情况下诱导的，事实上，在我们有任何意愿之前就诱导了。

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: Once in place, a defense mechanism such as tuning out takes on a life of its own. Little or nothing of a distressing nature need be there in the immediate environment for it to happen. It becomes, as it were, the“default” setting in the cerebral apparatus of awareness: unless some other special switch is turned on, tuned out will be the state that the brain automatically returns to. Because tuning out is based on deeply entrenched neurological responses, their later activation requires very little stimulus. Once a circuit is established, signals will travel along it much more easily than along alternative routes, in a manner analogous to the ease of walking along a beaten path rather than through grass or bush on either side of it,or water ﬂowing in a channel instead of across ﬂat ground. If we want the stream to run in a diﬀerent direction, we will have to create new courses for it. 一旦建立，像调出这样的防御机制就会自行发挥作用。即使周围环境没有令人痛苦的事情发生，它也会发生。可以说，它成为了大脑意识机制的“默认”设置：除非打开其他特殊开关，否则大脑会自动恢复到“调出”状态。由于“调出”是基于根深蒂固的神经反应，因此它们后来的激活只需要很少的刺激。一旦电路建立，信号沿着它比沿着替代路线更容易传播，就像沿着一条小路走比穿过它两侧的草丛或灌木丛，或者在渠道中流动比在平地上流动更容易一样。如果我们想让溪

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: For people deeply hurt, the internal world may oﬀer more meaning than the real one. A woman in her thirties whose ADD was never noticed because she was not hyperactive, only a day-dreamer, told me that she spent entire school days staring out the window, lost in fanciful adventures with imaginary friends. From the outside, one might have described her as“distracted.” e Latin root of distract is “draw away”—drawing her away from the inside was her hiddenmost emotional longing. Her brain unconsciously assigned greater value to a self-created internal universe than to anything or anyone in the classroom. 对于那些深受伤害的人来说，内心世界可能比现实世界更有意义。一位三十多岁的女性从未被注意到患有ADD，因为她不是多动症，而只是一个白日梦者，她告诉我，她在整个求学过程中都盯着窗外，沉浸在与想象中的朋友的异想天开的冒险中。从外界来看，她可能会被描述为“注意力不集中”。分散的拉丁词根是“拉走”——将她从内心深处拉走是她隐藏最深的情感渴望。她的大脑无意识地将更大的价值赋予了一个自我创造的内心世界，而不是课堂上的任何事物或任何人。

chapter: 14. Severed Thoughts and Flibbertigibbets: Distractibility and Tuning Out
text: e nagging hunger for emotional contact explains the oft-observed“paradox” that many children with ADD are capable of focused work in the presence of an adult who is keeping them company and paying attention to them. is is no paradox at all, if we see the opposing roles of anxiety and attachment in inﬂuencing attention: attachment promotes attention,anxiety undermines it. When the child is not concerned with seeking emotional contact, his prefrontal cortex is freed to allocate attention to the task at hand, illustrating that what we call attention deﬁcit disorder is not aﬁxed, unalterable physiological state; it’s a physiological state, yes, but notﬁxed and unalterable. e warmth and satisfaction of positive contact with the adult is often just as good as a psychostimulant in supplying the child’s prefrontal cortex with dopamine. Greater security means less anxiety and more focused attention. e unseen factor that remains constant in all situations is the child’s unconscious yearning for attachment, dating back to the ﬁrst years of life. Where this need is satisﬁed, ADD problems begin to recede. 对情感联系的强烈渴望解释了经常观察到的“悖论”，即许多患有注意力缺陷多动症（ADD）的儿童在有成年人陪伴并关注他们的情况下能够集中精力工作。如果我们看到焦虑和依恋在影响注意力方面的对立角色，那么这根本不是悖论：依恋促进注意力，焦虑破坏注意力。当孩子不关心寻求情感联系时，他的前额叶皮层就获得了自由，可以将注意力分配到手头的任务上，这表明我们所说的注意力缺陷障碍不是一种固定的、不可改变的生理状态；它是一种生理状态，是的，但不是固定的、不可改变的。与成人进行积极

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: I do not know if you have noticed that the moment you cease to be active, there is immediately a feeling of nervous apprehension; you feel as though you are not alive, notalert, so you must keep going. And there is fear of being alone, of going for a walk alone,of being by yourself, without a book, without a radio, without talking; the fear of sitting quietly without doing something all the time with your hands or with your mind or with your heart. 我不知道你是否注意过，当你不再活跃时，立刻会有一种紧张不安的感觉；你会觉得自己没有活着，没有警觉，所以你必须继续前进。还有害怕孤独，害怕独自散步，害怕独自一人，没有书，没有收音机，没有交谈；害怕静静地坐着，不做任何事情，无论是用你的手，用你的思想，还是用你的心。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: Hyperactivity is experienced in a number of ways. e person with ADD 多动症可以通过多种方式体验到。一个有注意力缺陷多动症的人feels discomfort at having to keep still for even short periods of time. ere may be a physical inability to refrain from restless movements for more than a few minutes. Always, one is caught in a mental whirlwind. A seventy-two-year-old man, a geologist, called it “newsreel thinking,” by which he meant the rapid shifting of his thoughts from one subject to another. (He had originally trained as an engineer but could not abide theconﬁnes of an oﬃce. He switched to geology because the work allowed him to be outdoors, on the move.) Another sign of hyperactivity may be frequent movement of the eyes, a scanning of the environment that frustrates other people. It is disconcerting to be with an individual who seems to be always on the lookout for something, or someone, else. 即使是短时间保持静止也会感到不适。这可能是因为身体无法在几分钟内抑制住不安分的动作。总是，一个人会陷入精神风暴。一位 72 岁的地质学家称其为“新闻片式思维”，他的意思是他的思维会从一件事迅速转移到另一件事上。（他最初接受的是工程师培训，但无法忍受办公室的束缚。他转向地质学是因为这项工作允许他在户外活动。）过度活跃的另一个表现可能是频繁地移动眼睛，对

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: ere is another component to hyperactivity: throughout life, it continues to be a human response during times of high anxiety. If you were told that in the next week, at some unpredictable moment, some unnamed disaster would strike you or one close to you, and that you were helpless to do anything to prevent it, your response would quite probably resemble the habitual mental and physical behaviors of the hyperactive child or adult with ADD. YOU would have diﬃculty focusing your thoughts, and your mind might feel like a squirrel on a treadmill: racing but not going anywhere. Sitting still would be a chore. A clichéd image of helpless anxiety in an adult is the father pacing nervously outside the delivery room where his wife is giving birth. I believe hyperactivity in ADD is fed by a current of permanent, subterranean anxiety. 这里是多动症另一个组成部分：在人的一生中，当处于高度焦虑状态时，多动症会持续存在。如果你被告知，在未来的一周内，在某个不可预知的时刻，某种不知名的灾难将会降临到你或你身边亲近的人身上，而且你对此无能为力，你的反应很可能会与多动症儿童或成人的惯常心理及身体行为类似。你会难以集中注意力，你的大脑可能会像在跑步机上的小松鼠一样：不停地跑，但就是到不了任何地方。坐着不动对你来说是一种折磨。父亲在产房外焦急不安地踱步，这是人们对成年人的刻板印象。我相信，ADD的过度活跃是由一股持续的、潜藏的焦虑情绪引发的。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: If hyperactivity expresses anxiety, lethargy and underarousal express shame. Shame, like anxiety, is an attachment emotion. “Whenever someone becomes signiﬁcant to us, whenever another’s caring, respect or valuing matters, the possibility for generating shame emerges,” writes the psychologist Gershen Kaufman.2 e origin of shame is the feeling of having been cut oﬀ from the parent, of having lost the connection, if only momentarily. It cannot be helped, it occurs unavoidably as part of maturing. 如果过度活跃表现的是焦虑，那么昏昏欲睡和反应迟钝表现的就是羞愧。和焦虑一样，羞愧也是一种依恋情绪。心理学家格申·考夫曼（Gershen Kaufman）写道：“只要一个人对我们来说变得重要，只要别人的关心、尊重或认可很重要，产生羞愧的可能性就会出现。”2羞愧的起源是感觉自己被父母抛弃，感觉自己失去了与父母的联系，哪怕这种联系只是暂时的。这是不可避免的，是成熟过程中的一部分。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: Shame becomes excessive if the parent’s signaling of disapproval is overly strong, or if the parent does not move to reestablish warm emotional contact with the child immediately—what Gershen Kaufman calls“restoring the interpersonal bridge.” Chronic stress experienced by the parent has the eﬀect of breaking that bridge. e small child does not have a large store of insight for interpreting the parent’s moods and facialexpressions: they either invite contact or forbid it. When the parent is distracted or withdrawn, the older infant or toddler experiences shame. Shame postures are observed in infants in response to nothing more than the parent breaking eye contact. e demeanor of the infants of depressed mothers is one of inactivity and the averted gaze. 如果父母表示不赞成的信号过于强烈，或者如果父母没有立即采取行动，重新与孩子建立温暖的情感联系——也就是格斯·考夫曼所说的“重新架起人际沟通的桥梁”——那么，羞耻感就会变得过度。父母长期承受的压力会破坏这种桥梁。年幼的孩子没有足够的洞察力来解读父母的情绪和面部表情：他们要么邀请接触，要么禁止接触。当父母心烦意乱或退缩时，年长一些的婴儿或幼儿就会感到羞耻。婴儿的羞耻姿态仅仅是因为父母中断了眼神接触而产生的。抑郁母亲的孩子的行为是消极的，会回避他人的目光。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: Past the toddler phase, there will be many times the child’s behavior may trigger an angry response from the parent, the ADD child more than the average. Some parents are able to express anger without making the child feel cut oﬀ emotionally. ey convey disapproval without rejection. Otherparents, especially those with self-regulation problems of their own, may react with open or choked rage, punishing coldness or dejected withdrawal that signals defeat and disappointment. ese were the anger responses my children experienced from me. Each time this happens, shame is evoked in the child, especially as the parent usually believes—and makes the childbelieve—that whatever his (the parent’s) reaction is, the child is responsible for it. 在幼儿阶段之后，孩子的行为可能会多次引发父母的愤怒反应，多动症儿童比普通儿童更多。一些父母能够表达愤怒，而不会让孩子感到情感上的疏离。有些父母，尤其是那些自身存在自我调节问题的父母，可能会做出公开或隐忍的愤怒反应，以冷漠或沮丧的退缩来惩罚孩子，这表明他们感到挫败和失望。这些就是我的孩子从我这里感受到的愤怒反应。每次发生这种情况，孩子都会感到羞愧，特别是父母通常会认为——并让孩子也这样认为——无论他（父母）做出什么反应，都是孩子的错。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: e deep feelings of shame associated with attention deﬁcit disorder are usually explained by the obvious fact that the ADD individual gets many things wrong. On the face of it, this makes sense. e adult or child with attention deﬁcit disorder may frequently oﬀend people or break a promise or be late somewhere. Given his inattentiveness and diﬃculties reading nonverbal social messages, he treads on toes—in both senses of that phrase. He carries memories of having failed at many tasks, of being deservedlycriticized—so he thinks—for many shortcomings. Such events, however,can only reinforce shame or provoke it—they cannot cause it. Its origins have nothing to do with bad deeds, failures or hurting anyone. Like its opposite number, hyperactivity, shame began as a normal physiological state that escaped regulation by the cortex. It becomes wound tightly into the self-identity of the individual. 与注意力缺陷障碍相关的深切的羞耻感通常可以用这样一个显而易见的事实来解释：患有注意力缺陷障碍的个体做错了很多事情。从表面上看，这是有道理的。患有注意力缺陷障碍的成人或儿童可能会经常冒犯他人、违背诺言或迟到。鉴于其注意力涣散和难以理解非言语社交信息，他会无意中冒犯他人——无论是字面意思还是引申义。他会记得自己在许多任务中失败，并认为自己理应因为许多缺点而受到批评。然而，这些事件只能强化羞耻感或激起羞耻感，而不会导致羞耻感。羞耻感的起源与不良

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: 行为、失败或伤害任何人无关。与注意力缺陷障碍相反，羞耻感最初是一种不受大脑皮层控制的正常生理状态，它与个体自我认同紧密地交织在一起。John Ratey has aptly observed that “I’m sorry” is the most common phrase in the vocabulary of attention deﬁcit disorder. What strikes me immediately when I meet new ADD patients is how often they apologize. ey apologize when I ask them to speak louder, when they cannot easily answer a question, when I interrupt their ﬂow of speech to ask for moreinformation, when I tell them that we will wind up the session in a few minutes as time is running out. People ask forgiveness for being in myoﬃce in the ﬁrst place. eir opening words may be an apology: “I am sorry to be taking up your time. I am sure there are many people waiting to see you who need help a lot more than I do.” Of course, they also apologize if they think they have too serious a problem: “I’m sorry, I know it’sdiﬃcult to help me. You couldn’t have imagined you would be dealing with such a basket case.” ese expressions of remorse, where no oﬀense wascommitted, communicate a deep sense of shame. If the words did not betray shame, it could still be recognizable in the averted eyes. 约翰·瑞迪恰如其分地观察到，“对不起”是注意力缺陷障碍患者最常用的短语。当我遇到新的ADD患者时，最令我震惊的是他们道歉的频率。当我要求他们说话更大声时，他们道歉；当他们无法轻松回答问题时，他们道歉；当我打断他们的讲话以获取更多信息时，他们道歉；当我告诉他们时间不多了，我们几分钟后就要结束会谈

text: 时，他们道歉。人们首先请求原谅的是占用我的办公室。他们的开场白可能是道歉：“占用您的时间，我很抱歉。”我确信有很多人在等着见你，他们需要的帮助远比我多。”当然，如果他们认为自己的问题太严重了，他们也会道歉：“对不起，我知道这很难帮助我。你无法想象你会处理这样一个烂摊子。”这些没有冒犯的悔恨表达传达了一种深深的羞耻感。如果这些话没有透露出羞耻感，那么在回避的目光中仍然可以认出羞耻感。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: ADD swings back and forth between over-the-top, purposeless excitement and a nonrestful vegetative state in which the predominant emotion is shame. Some tend to get stuck at one or the other of these opposite poles.e two states may also be present at the same time, resulting in agitated,unfocused inactivity. ADD在过度、无目的的兴奋和不安的植物状态之间来回摇摆，植物状态的主要情绪是羞耻。有些人倾向于在这些相反的极点之一停滞不前。这两种状态也可能同时出现，导致不安、注意力不集中的无活动状态。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: Like so much else about attention deﬁcit disorder, hyperactivity,lethargy and shame are closely connected with the neurological memories of the distant, stressed or distracted caregiver. ere will be a sense of discomfort as soon as the mind becomes aware of itself, because such awareness immediately triggers responses encoded with the infant’s distress at feeling emotionally alone. e mind then lapses into helpless lethargy, or races away, looking for something to attach to: some idea, some fantasy,some memory, conversation, music, reading—anything. When it cannot do so, there is intense unease—or the aversion to one’s own mind, which we call boredom. 与注意力缺陷障碍的许多其他症状一样，过度活跃、昏昏欲睡和羞耻感与照顾者遥远、紧张或心不在焉的神经记忆密切相关。一旦意识意识到自己，就会产生一种不适感，因为这种意识会立即引发与婴儿独自感受情感痛苦相关的编码反应。然后，意识就会陷入无助的昏睡，或者寻找一些东西来依附：一些想法、一些幻想、一些记忆、对话、音乐、阅读——任何东西。当它无法做到这一点时，就会产生强烈的不安——或者厌恶自己的意识，我们称之为无聊。

chapter: 15. The Pendulum Swings: Hyperactivity, Lethargy and Shame
text: A requirement of healing, becoming whole, is circuitry in the brain that can carry diﬀerent messages and a diﬀerent, nonhelpless image of the self. ere is strong evidence that such circuits can develop at any time inlife, as can neural pathways to help the cortex to do its job of inhibition and regulation. 愈合、变得完整的一个要求是大脑中的回路，它可以传递不同的信息，并产生一个不同的、不无助的自我形象。有强有力的证据表明，这些回路可以在生命中的任何时候发展，就像帮助大脑皮层完成抑制和调节功能的神经通路一样。

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: It is not curing that ADD children need: they need to be helped to grow. What is required is not a change in parenting techniques but a change in parenting attitudes, based on a deeper understanding of the child. e adult with attention deﬁcit disorder needs also to gain a deeper understanding of herself, to undertake the task we will later describe as self-parenting.

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: 治疗多动症儿童需要的不是治愈：他们需要被帮助成长。我们需要的不是改变育儿技巧，而是改变育儿态度，基于对孩子有更深入的了解。患有注意力缺陷障碍的成年人也需要对自己有更深入的了解，承担起我们将在后面描述的自我养育的任务。

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: Integration of cognition withemotion—the melding of what we know with what we feel—is the very integration the healing process in ADD requires. Lack of it underlies the fragmentation of the ADD mind.

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: 认知与情感的整合——我们所知道的事情与我们的感受的融合——正是ADD的治愈过程所需要的一体化。缺乏这种整合导致了ADD思维的碎片化。

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: understandable desire of parents is for point-by-point advice: What do I do in this situation? How do I handle that? Important as such questions are,they are secondary. e answers to them depend on how one interprets the child’s behaviors and on what the long-term objectives are. What we want to promote is not a mere change of behavior but a transformation of inner experience leading to the development of self-regulation. 父母希望得到逐条建议是可以理解的：在这种情况下我该怎么办？我该如何处理？虽然这些问题很重要，但它们是次要的。e对这些问题的回答取决于一个人如何解释孩子的行为以及长期目标是什么。我们想要促进的不仅仅是行为上的改变，而是内心体验的转变，从而导致自我调节的发展。

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: Every child with ADD has been wounded by a disruption in the 每个患有注意力缺陷多动症的孩子都受到了干扰的伤害。relationship between the caregiver and the sensitive infant. All the behaviors and mental patterns of attention deﬁcit disorder are external signs of the wound, or ineﬃcient defenses against feeling the pain of it. If development is to take place, energy has to be liberated for growth that now is consumed in protecting the self from further hurt. e key factor is cementing the attachment relationship. 照顾者与敏感婴儿之间的关系。注意力缺陷障碍的所有行为和心理模式都是创伤的外部迹象，或者是对感受创伤的无效防御。如果发展要发生，就必须释放能量以促进成长，而目前成长正消耗在保护自己免受进一步伤害上。关键因素是巩固依恋关系。

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: 戴蒙德博士写道：“我们，重要的是要刺激大脑中引发情感表达的部分。在任何年龄，满足情感需求都是至关重要的。”7

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: In human brains, the circuitry of reason and emotion are closelyconnected, which is why troubled relationships lead directly to diﬃculties in brain processing. ey are not the only cause of disorganized thinking,but they are by far the commonest cause. Restoring relationships on a healthy basis promotes mental organization. New ways of processing emotions need new neural circuits, and the wiring of new circuits requires new experiences in a favorable emotional milieu. e relationship with the parents is the earth, the rain, the sun and the shade in which the child’s mental development must blossom

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: 在人类的大脑中，理性与情感的回路是紧密相连的，这就是为什么混乱的人际关系会直接导致大脑处理困难。它们不是思维混乱的唯一原因，但它们是最常见的原因。在健康的基础上恢复人际关系会促进精神组织。处理情感的新方法需要新的神经回路，而新回路的布线需要在有利的情感环境中获得新的经验。与父母的关系是大地、雨水、阳光和阴影，孩子的精神发展必须在其中绽放。

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: In his book On Becoming a Person, Carl Rogers described a warm,caring attitude, for which he adopted the phrase unconditional positive regard because, he said, “It has no conditions of worth attached to it.” is is a caring, wrote Rogers, “which is not possessive, which demands no personal gratiﬁcation. It is an atmosphere which simply demonstrates Icare; not I care for you if you behave thus and so.”8 So the ﬁrst thing is to create some space in the child’s heart of hearts for the certainty that she is precisely the person the parents want and love. She does not have to doanything, or be any diﬀerent, to earn that love—in fact, she cannot doanything, because the love cannot be won and cannot be lost. It is not conditional. It is completely independent of the child’s behavior. It is justthere, regardless of which side the child is acting from, “good” or “bad.”e child can be ornery, unpleasant, whiny, uncooperative and plain rude,and the parent still lets her feel loved. Ways have to be found to let the child know that certain behaviors are unacceptable, without making the child herself feel not accepted. She has to be able to bring her unrest, her least likable side, to the parent without fear that it would threaten the relationship. When that is made possible, absolute security is established. We can reliably expect emotional growth to follow. 在《成为一个人》一书中，卡尔·罗杰斯描述了一种温暖、关爱的态度，他采用“无条件积极关注”这个短语来描述，因为，他说，“它没有附加任何有价值的条件。”罗杰斯写道，这是一种关爱，“不是占有性的，不要求个人的感激。它是一种

chapter: 16. It Ain’t Over Till It’s Over: Unconditional Positive Regard
text: 氛围，只是表现出我在乎你；不是因为你表现好我才在乎你。”因此，首先要在孩子的内心深处创造一些空间，让孩子确信自己正是父母所希望和爱戴的人。她不需要做任何事情，或者成为任何不同的人，就能赢得这份爱——事实上，她什么也不用做，因为这份爱不会被赢得，也不会被失去。它不是有条件的。它完全独立于孩子的行为。它就在那里，无论孩子是从“好”的一方还是从“坏”的一方表现出来。孩子可能会脾气暴躁、令人讨厌、发牢骚、不合作和无礼，而父母仍然让她感受到被爱。必须找到方法，让孩子知道某些行为是不可接受的，而不会让孩子自己感到不被接受。她必须能够向父母表达她的不安，她最不讨人喜欢的一面，而不用担心这会威胁到这段关系。当这成为可能时，绝对的安全感就建立了。我们可以可靠地期待情感上的成长。

chapter: 17. Wooing the Child
text: Shame, as we have seen, is the physiological-emotional state resulting from the sense of being isolated, cut oﬀ. e ADD child is mired in shame. 正如我们所看到的，羞耻是一种生理-情感状态，是由被孤立、被切断的感觉引起的，ADD儿童陷入羞耻的泥潭。

chapter: 18. Like Fish in the Sea
text: As we have said, self-regulation is the goal of development; the lack of it is the fundamental impairment in ADD. One way of describing self-regulation is to say that it is the ability to maintain the internal environment within a functional and safe range, regardless of external circumstance. On the emotional level, the self-regulation of moods means that neither despondency nor uncontrolled exuberance, neither passive submission nor blind rage, control the mind. A person can experiencefrustration, disappointment or sadness without being seized by despair. Happiness does not need to be euphoria or anger hostility. text: Self-regulation is intimately connected with a process developmental psychology has called individuation, or diﬀerentiation. Individuation—becoming a self-motivating, self-accepting person, a true individual—is the ultimate goal of development. As individuation unfolds, children are able to move more and more independently into the world, impelled by their own interests and needs. Less and less do they require that another person see exactly what they see in order to feel validated, or that another person feel exactly what they feel. ey may have needs and desire for closeness,warmth and mutual support with another human being, but they do not need to be emotionally fused with the other person—they can function on their own, if need be. 自我调节与一个发展心理学过程密切相关，该过程被称为个体化，或差异化。个体化——成为一个自我激励、自我接纳的人，一个真正的个体——是发展的最终目标。随着个体化的展开，孩子们能够越来越独立地进入这个世界，受到他们自己的兴趣和需求的驱使。他们越来越不需要让另一个人看到他们所看到的东西，以获得认可，或者让另一个人感受到他们所感受到的东西。他们可能有与另一个人亲近、温暖和相互支持的需要和愿望，但他们不需要与另一个人在情感上融合——如果有必要，他们可以独立发挥作用。

chapter: 20. The Defiant Ones Oppositionality
text: Counterwill is an automatic resistance put up by a human being with an incompletely developed sense of self, a reﬂexive and unthinking opposition to the will of the other. It is a natural but immature resistance arising from the fear of being controlled. Counterwill arises in anyone who has not yet developed a mature and conscious will of her own. Although it can remain active throughout life, normally it makes its most dramatic appearance during the toddler phase and again in adolescence. In manypeople, and in the vast majority of children with ADD, it becomes entrenched as an ever-present force and may remain powerfully active well into adulthood. It immensely complicates personal relationships, school performance and job or career success. “逆抗意志”是一种由自我意识尚未完全成熟的人所产生的自动抵抗行为，这种抵抗是对他人意志的一种无意识、本能性的反对。它源于对被控制的恐惧，因此是一种自然但尚不成熟的抵抗机制。任何尚未形成成熟、自觉的自我意志的人都会产生这种逆抗意志。虽然这种心理现象可能伴随人的一生，但它通常在幼儿期和青春期表现得最为明显。在许多人身上，尤其是在大多数患有多动症的孩子中，这种逆抗意志会逐渐固化为一股持续存在的力量，并可能一直活跃到成年期。它极大地扰乱了人际关系、学业表现以及职业发展。

chapter: 20. The Defiant Ones Oppositionality
text: Counterwill has many manifestations. e parent of a child with attention deﬁcit disorder will be familiar with them. Most obviously, it is expressed in verbal resistance—“I don’t have to,” “You can’t make me,” the constant arguing and countering whatever the parent proposes, the ubiquitous “You are not the boss of me.” Like a psychological immunesystem, counterwill functions to keep out anything that does not originate within the child herself. It is present when the four-year-old puts both hands over his ears to keep out the parent’s voice, or when the older child pins up an angry Keep Out sign on her door. It is visible in the body language of the adolescent and teenager: the sullen look and the shrugged shoulder. Its signs drive some adults around the bend, as in the futile “I’ll wipe that smirk oﬀ your face” of many a parent or teacher. Counterwill is also expressed through passivity. Every parent of an ADD child has had the experience of feeling intense frustration when, being pressured for time,they have tried to hurry their son or daughter along. e greater the parent’s anxiety and the greater the pressure he puts on the child, the more slothfully slow the child seems to become. Passivity begins to look like almost second nature to some of these children, although when she is highly motivated, the child will perform many tasks with alacrity. ispassivity, what people may call laziness, can signal a strong internal resistance. 反抗意志有多种表现形式。有注意力缺陷障碍孩子的父母应该对此非常熟悉。最明显的表现就是言语上的抗拒——“我不想做”，“你不能强迫我”；无论父母提出什么建议，孩子都会不断反驳；还有那句屡见不鲜的

chapter: 20. The Defiant Ones Oppositionality
text: Like all natural phenomena and all stages in the child’s life, counterwill has a positive purpose. It ﬁrst appears in the toddler to help in the task of individuating, of beginning to separate from the parent. In essence, the child erects a wall of no’s. Behind this wall, the child can gradually learn her likes and dislikes, aversions or preferences,without being overwhelmed by the far more powerful force generated by the parent’s will. Counterwill may be likened to the small fence one places around a tender young shoot to protect it from being eaten. e vulnerable little plant here is the child’s will. Without that protective fence, it cannot survive. In adolescence, counterwill serves the same goal, helping the young person loosen his psychological dependence on the family. It comes at a time when the sense of self is having to emerge out of the cocoon of the family. It is a defense mechanism to protect this fragile, threatened sense of self. By keeping out the parent’s expectations and demands,counterwill helps to make room for the growth of the child’s own self-generated motivations and preferences.

chapter: 20. The Defiant Ones Oppositionality
text: 就像所有自然现象以及儿童成长过程中的各个阶段一样，“反抗意志”也有其积极的意义。这种意志最初出现在学步期的儿童身上，它的作用在于帮助儿童实现自我认同，开始与父母分离。实际上，儿童是通过建立起这层“拒绝的屏障”来逐渐了解自己的喜好与厌恶之处的。在这道屏障的保护下，儿童不必受到父母意志力的压制，从而能够自由地发展自己的意愿。这种反抗意志，就好比人们为脆弱的嫩芽搭建的小围栏，用来防止它们被吃掉一样。而这里所谓的“脆弱植物”，其实就是儿童的意志力；没有这道保护性的“围栏”，儿童的意志力就无法存活下去。在青春期，这种“反抗意志”发挥着同样的作用——帮助青少年摆脱对家庭的心理依赖。这一阶段，个体的自我意识正试图从家庭的束缚中逐渐萌芽出来。这种反抗意志实际上是一种防御机制，用来保护这种脆弱而容易受到威胁的自我意识。通过抵制父母的期望与要求，反抗意志为孩子自身产生的动力和偏好提供了成长空间。

chapter: 20. The Defiant Ones Oppositionality
text: underdevelopment. e weaker the child—or, for that matter, the adult—is psychologically, the more automatic and rigid the counterwill response becomes. A strong unconscious defense indicates a weak, undeveloped will,which is what is reﬂected in the oppositionality that seems intrinsic—but only seems that way—to the ADD personality. A strong defense is there only because there is threat, and the child is threatened only because a strong sense of his own self has not developed suﬃciently. So the root of the problem is that rather than being too powerful, the inner core of self, the true will, is stunted. is is why the various epithets such as stubborn,willful and so on indicate not a strong will but the lack of one. An emotionally self-conﬁdent person does not have to adopt an oppositional stance automatically. She may resist others’ attempts to control her, but she will not do so rigidly and defensively. If she opposes something, it is from a strong sense of what her true preferences are, not a knee-jerk reﬂex. A child not driven by counterwill does not automatically experience any advice,any expression of the parent’s opinion, as an attempt at control. Registering deep in her psyche is a sense of solidity about this inner core, this nucleus of the self, so there is no necessity to defend the will against being overwhelmed. I will be able to hang on to myself, an inner voice reassuresher, even if I listen to what somebody else thinks, or do what someone else wants me to do. I won’t lose my identity, so I don’t have to protect myself through resistance. I can aﬀord to cooperate. I can aﬀord to heed. Incontrast, the counterwill of the child with an underdeveloped self asserts itself ferociously.

text: Helping the child to label her feelings in words is what was referred to as symbolization when we discussed counterwill. It is also an important step in promoting autonomy. Words are symbols. ey stand for feelings and actions. Without the capacity to put things into symbols, children are driven to act out every strong feeling and every urge—it is the only way they can express themselves. ey are thus unable to take charge ofthemselves, impelled as they are to act by emotions they cannot identify. Without learning to symbolize emotions they are also likely to experience everything in terms of simple and opposing categories: people are alternately mean or nice, good or bad. It’s either “I love you, Mommy” or“I hate you.” e child has greater autonomy, a greater choice of possibleresponses, when she can say, “I didn’t like what Mrs. So-and-so said to me in class today,” than when she is restricted to “Mrs. So-and-so is mean.” Language supports freedom, including freedom from one’s own impulses. 当我们讨论反意志时，帮助孩子用语言表达自己的感受就是所谓的象征化。这也是促进自主性发展的重要一步。语言是符号，它们代表感受和行为。如果没有把事物符号化的能力，孩子们就会被迫表达自己强烈的感受和冲动——这是他们表达自己的唯一方式。因此，他们无法掌控自己，无法控制由他们无法识别的情绪驱使的行为。如果不学会把

chapter: 22. My Marshmallow Caught Fire: Motivation and Autonomy
text: e process of becoming connected with other people and learning appropriate humaninteractions, of developing into a social creature, is called socialization. Children don’t have to be trained into socialization. Because it is a fundamental human drive, we naturally develop connectedness and compassion if our own basic needs have been respected. Socialization is at the apex of a pyramid. e base is formed by secure attachment and autonomy. We often make the mistake with our children of puttingsocialization—the rules of social conduct, what is called “good behavior”—ahead of attachment and individuation. We try to make our kids act as truly socially responsible people at the expense of their emotional security and their autonomous sense of self. is may result in compliance, but not in the internal, organic growth of true morality and social responsibility. We can no more foster genuine socialization this way than we can balance a pyramid on its apex, upside down.

chapter: 25. Justifying One’s Existence: Self-Esteem
text: Since having a strong core self relies on acceptance of feelings, being out of touch with the emotional side puts a person out of touch with herself. What then remains to be esteemed? Only a false self, a concoction of what we would like to imagine ourselves to be and what we have divined others want us to be. Sooner or later, people come to realize that this false self—wanting what they think they should want, feeling what they think they should feel—does not work for them. When they look inside themselves, they discover a frightening emptiness, a vacuum, an absence of a true self or of intrinsic motivation. Many a time I have heard ADD adults say, “I don’t know who I am,” or, “I don’t know what I want to do in my life.”

chapter: 26. Memories Are Made of This
text: As the Harvard psychiatrist Judith Lewis Herman has pointed out, “To some degree everyone is a prisoner of the past.”1 Without knowing it, we often relive the past. What we take for present-day reality represents, in many situations, reactivated early memories stored in the implicit memorysystem, a vast and infallibly accurate record of past experiences. Implicit memory happens, according to the psychologist and memory researcher Daniel Schacter, “when people are inﬂuenced by a past experience without any awareness that they are remembering.”2 Unconscious emotions and conscious feelings, rapid shifts in mood and dramatic physiological changes in the body can occur under the impact of implicit memory. 正如哈佛精神病学家朱迪思·刘易斯·赫尔曼所指出的那样，“在某种程度上，每个人都是过去经历的囚徒。”1 我们常常在不经意间重温过去。在许多情况下，我们所认为的当下现实，代表的是存储于内隐记忆系统中的早期记忆被重新激活。内隐记忆是过去经历的庞大而准确无误的记录。根据心理学家、记忆研究专家丹尼尔·谢克特（Daniel Schacter）的说法，“当人们受到过去经历的影响，却丝毫没有意识到自己在回忆时，内隐记忆就发生了。”2 在内隐记忆的影响下，潜意识情感和意识情感、情绪的快速变化以及身体的剧烈生理变化都有可能发生。

text: Trevor’s anxiety is not over the ending of the relationship—he is serially ending relationships—but over being the one who is left by the other. When mother and infant are rapturously gazing into each other’s eyes, the infant at some point will look away, to avoid being overstimulated. He has no anxiety over doing so. Should the mother be the one to break eyecontact, however, the infant is mortiﬁed and is immediately swept into the physiological state of shame. Trevor’s desperation to avoid that state is based on his implicit memories of it. e circuits activated whenever he fears being left are those encoded with the emotions Trevor ﬁrst experienced when, as a highly sensitive infant, he did not receive theunqualiﬁed and undivided loving attention he needed and craved. In this way he remembers what did not happen. 特雷弗的焦虑不在于关系的结束——他一直在结束一段段关系——而在于被对方抛弃。当母亲和婴儿陶醉地凝视着彼此的双眼时，婴儿会在某个时刻将目光移开，以避免受到过度刺激。他不会因为移开目光而感到焦虑。然而，如果母亲先移开目光，婴儿就会感到羞愧，并立刻陷入一种羞耻的生理状态。特雷弗竭力避免这种状态，是因为他对这种状态有着根深蒂固的记忆。每当他担心被抛弃时，他的边缘系统就会被激活，而这种情绪正是特雷弗在孩提时代第一次经历时所编码的。当时他还是一个高度敏感的婴儿，没有得到他所需要和渴望的无条件、无保留的关爱。通过这种方式，他记住了那些未曾发生的事情。

I never want to feel that hurt again. 鲍尔比还指出，由于压力、焦虑、抑郁或忙于其他事情，父母虽然身在孩子身边，但情感上却可能缺席。从婴儿的角度来看，这无关紧要。他的编码反应是一样的，因为对他来说，真正的问题不是父母是否在场，而是父母是否情感上可以亲近。鲍尔比将这种退缩动态称为“防御性疏离”，它的含义是：“你的缺席对我来说太伤人了，以至于我将用坚硬的情感外壳把自己包裹起来，对爱——因而对痛苦——无动于衷。我再也不想感受到这种伤害了。”

chapter: 27. Remembering What Didn’t Happen: The ADD Relationship
text: An individual with ADD choosing a partner on the same plane of 有注意力缺陷障碍的人在同一平面上选择伴侣psychological growth as herself is unavoidable. Since ADD by deﬁnition implies underdeveloped emotional intelligence, any such relationship, also by deﬁnition, will begin with two people who have both been stuck at fairly early stages of emotional development. Although, as with every other aspect of ADD, there will be a broad range of variation, no ADD relationship will avoid the problems arising from the mutual lack of maturity. Bymaturity, I mean here the degree of individuation, the capacity of the person to genuinely sustain herself emotionally during diﬃcult times without having to be mothered or fathered by someone else.

chapter: 第1章
text: Never at rest, the mind of the ADD adult flits about like some deranged bird that can light here or there for a while but is perched nowhere long enough to make a home.患有多动症的成年人，他们的大脑永远处于活跃状态，就像那些行为紊乱的鸟儿一样：它们可能会在这里或那里短暂停留，但却无法在任何一处久留下来，从而建立起自己的“家园”。

chapter: 第1章
text: The shock of self-recognition many adults experience on learning about ADD is both exhilarating and painful. It gives coherence, for the first time, to humiliations and failures, to plans unfulfilled and promises unkept, to gusts of manic enthusiasm that consume themselves in their own mad dance, leaving emotional debris in their wake, to the seemingly limitless disorganization of activities, of brain, car, desk, room.许多成年人在了解到自己患有注意力缺陷多动障碍后，所体验到的那种自我认知带来的冲击既令人振奋，又令人痛苦。这种冲击使得那些曾经的羞辱与失败、那些未能实现的计划与违背的承诺、那些被狂热情绪所吞噬、最终只留下情感碎片的行为，以及那些看似无序的生活状态——无论是个人的生活安排，还是大脑、汽车、书桌或房间的整理状况——都第一次获得了某种逻辑上的连贯性。

chapter: 第1章
text: Beyond everything, recognition revealed the reason for my lifelong sense of somehow never approaching my potential in terms of self-expression and self-definition—the ADD adult’s awareness that he has talents or insights or some undefinable positive quality he could perhaps connect with if the wires weren’t crossed.最重要的是，这种认可让我明白了为什么自己一生中总感觉在自我表达与自我认知方面始终无法充分发挥自己的潜力——对于患有注意力缺陷多动障碍的成年人来说，他们清楚地知道自己拥有某些天赋、见解，或者某些难以用语言定义的积极特质，只要那些干扰因素不存在，自己或许就能够将这些特质充分发挥出来。

chapter: 第1章
text: ADD has much to do with pain, present in every one of the adults and children who have come to me for assessment. The deep emotional hurt they carry is telegraphed by the downcast, averted eyes, the rapid, discontinuous flow of speech, the tense body postures, the tapping feet and fidgety hands and by the nervous, self-deprecating humor.注意力缺陷障碍与疼痛有着密切的关系——所有前来我这里接受评估的成人和儿童，都存在着这种疼痛。他们内心所承受的深刻情感创伤，会通过以下表现显现出来：低垂的双眼、断断续续的言语、紧张的身体姿势、不停踢腿或摆弄双手的行为，以及那些充满紧张情绪、带有自我贬低意味的幽默表达。

chapter: 第1章
text: At times I have wished that the “experts” and media pundits who deny the existence of attention deficit disorder could meet only a few of the severely affected adults who have sought my help. These men and women, in their thirties, forties and fifties, have never been able to maintain any sort of a long-term job or profession.有时候，我真希望那些否认注意力缺陷障碍存在的“专家”以及媒体评论员们，能够去见见那些曾向我寻求帮助的、病情严重的成年人。这些三四十岁、甚至五十多岁的男女，从来都无法从事任何一份能够持续较长时间的职业。

chapter: 第1章
text: Their moods fly back and forth from lethargy and dejection to agitation. The creative talents they have been blessed with have not been pursued. They are intensely frustrated at what they perceive as their failures. Their self-esteem is lost in some deep well. Most often they are firm in the conviction that their problems are the result of a basic, incorrigible flaw in their personalities.他们的情绪在昏昏欲睡、沮丧与焦躁不安之间反复波动。他们所拥有的那些创造天赋始终没有得到充分发挥；对于自己所认为的那些“失败”，他们感到极为沮丧。他们的自尊心早已荡然无存。大多数时候，他们都坚信，自己遇到的所有问题都是由于自身性格中存在某些根本性的、无法改正的缺陷所导致的。

chapter: 第1章
text: This absence of mind is one cause of the distractibility and short attention spans that bedevil the adult or child with ADD, except around activities of high interest and motivation.这种注意力不集中的现象，正是导致患有多动症的成年人或儿童容易分心、注意力难以持久的原因之一；不过，在那些让他们感到非常感兴趣、有强烈动机的活动中，这种情况就不会出现。

chapter: 第1章
text: ADD is situational: in the same individual its expression may vary greatly from one circumstance to another. There are certain classes, for example, in which the ADD child may perform remarkably well, while in others she is scattered, unproductive and perhaps disruptive.注意力缺陷障碍具有情境依赖性：对于同一个个体来说，其在不同情境下的表现可能会存在很大差异。例如，在某些特定情境下，患有注意力缺陷障碍的儿童可能会表现得非常出色；而在其他情境中，他们则可能会变得注意力分散、效率低下，甚至会扰乱正常的秩序。

chapter: 第1章
text: The individual with ADD experiences the mind as a perpetual-motion machine. An intense aversion to boredom, an abhorrence of it, takes hold as soon as there is no ready focus of activity, distraction or attention. An unremitting lack of stillness is felt internally—a constant background static in the brain, a ceaseless “white noise,” as Dr. John Ratey, a Harvard psychiatrist, has put患有注意力缺陷多动障碍的人会觉得自己的大脑就像一台永远在运转的机器。一旦没有可以集中注意力去进行的活动或事物，他们就会对无聊产生强烈的厌恶感。在内心深处，他们会持续感受到一种不安宁的状态——大脑中仿佛存在着持续的“背景噪音”，这种噪音永无止息，正如哈佛大学的精神病学家约翰·雷蒂博士所描述的那样。

chapter: 第1章
text: I, for one, have rarely had a moment’s relaxation without the immediate and troubling feeling that I ought to be doing something else instead.就我而言，每当我有片刻的放松时光时，总会立刻感到不安，觉得自己应该去做其他事情才对。The restlessness coexists with long periods of procrastination. The threat of failure or the promise of reward has to be immediate for the motivation apparatus to be turned on. Without the rousing adrenaline rush of racing against time, inertia prevails.这种坐立不安的情绪与长时间的拖延行为并存。只有当失败带来的威胁或成功带来的奖励具有即时性时，人的动机系统才会被激活。如果没有与时间赛跑所带来的那种令人兴奋的肾上腺素激增，惰性就会占据上风。

chapter: 第1章
text: An adult with ADD looks back on his life to see countless plans never fully realized and intentions unfulfilled. “I am a person of permanent potential,” one patient said. Surges of initial enthusiasm quickly ebb.患有注意力缺陷多动障碍的成年人在回顾自己的人生时会发现，自己有无数计划始终未能完全实现，许多初衷也未能达成。“我其实是一个永远充满潜力的人，”一位患者这样说道。然而，最初的热情往往很快就会消退殆尽。

chapter: 第1章
text: The ADD mind is afflicted by a sort of time illiteracy, or what Dr. Russell Barkley has called “time blindness.” One is either hopelessly short of time, dashing about like a deaf bat, or else acts as if blessed with the gift of eternity. It’s as if one’s time sense never developed past a stage other people leave behind in early childhood.

chapter: 第1章
text: 患有注意力缺陷多动障碍的人，其时间感知能力存在某种缺陷，或者用拉塞尔·巴克利博士的话来说，就是“时间盲”。这些人要么会觉得时间严重不足，像一只瞎了眼的蝙蝠一样手忙脚乱；要么就会表现得好像自己被赐予了永生的能力一样，完全不担心时间的限制。他们的时间感知能力似乎永远停留在了其他人在幼儿时期就已经超越的那个发展阶段。

text: The brain, flooded with multiple bits of sensory data, thoughts, feelings and impulses, cannot focus, and the mind or body cannot be still.当大脑接收到大量感官信息、各种想法、情感以及冲动时，它就无法集中注意力，身心也会变得无法平静下来。

chapter: 第1章
text: This sharing of emotional spaces is called attunement.这种情感空间的共享被称为“情感同步”。

chapter: 第1章
text: Attachment is simply our need to be close to somebody. It represents the absolute need of the utterly and helplessly vulnerable human infant for secure closeness with at least one nourishing, protective and constantly available parenting figure.依恋，其实就是我们与某人保持亲密关系的需求。对于那些极其脆弱、无助的人类婴儿来说，这种需求尤为迫切——他们绝对需要与至少一位能够给予他们关爱、保护，并始终愿意陪伴在他们身边的养育者建立亲密的关系。

chapter: 第1章
text: Curiously, I felt much more like myself. It was as if a fog had evaporated and I saw that for years previously I’d had only periodic glimpses of a life not burdened by negative feelings.奇怪的是，我突然感觉自己重新找回了真正的自我。仿佛有一层迷雾终于消散了，我这才意识到：在过去的那些年里，我其实只是偶尔才能瞥见那种没有负面情绪困扰的生活。

chapter: 第1章
text: The skill of attention that begins during the initial stages of brain growth and mental development goes through several important phases, but the central buttress of them all is the secure attachment/attunement relationship with the primary caregiver.注意力这种能力在人类大脑开始发育、心智开始形成的初期阶段就已开始形成，并会经历几个重要的发展阶段；而其中最为关键的因素，就是与主要照顾者之间建立起安全、稳定的依恋关系。

chapter: 第1章
text: Individuation—becoming a self-motivating, self-accepting person, a true individual—is the ultimate goal of development. As individuation unfolds, children are able to move more and more independently into the world, impelled by their own interests and needs. Less and less do they require that another person see exactly what they see in order to feel validated, or that another person feel exactly what they feel.个体化——成为一个具有自我驱动力、能够自我接纳的人，成为一个真正的独立个体——才是发展的最终目标。随着个体化进程的推进，孩子们会逐渐以更加独立的方式融入这个世界，他们的行动完全受自身兴趣和需求的驱使。他们越来越不再需要依赖他人来理解自己所看到的东西，也不再需要他人能够感受到自己所感受到的情感。

chapter: 第1章
text: Every criticism they hear, every blaming word—anything they interpret as at all judgmental—activates in them feelings of shame, which they try to defend themselves against with all their might.他们听到的每一句批评，每一句指责之词——任何他们认为带有评判意味的话语——都会在他们心中激起羞耻感，而他们会竭尽全力来抵御这种感觉。

chapter: 第1章
text: People who have a grandiose and inflated view of themselves on the conscious level are lacking true self-esteem at the core of their psyche. Their exaggerated self-evaluation is a defense against their deepest feelings of worthlessness.那些在意识层面上对自己抱有过于夸大、不切实际的看法的人，其心理深处其实缺乏真正的自尊。他们那种夸张的自我评价，其实是一种用来抵御自己内心深处那种无价值感的防御机制。

chapter: 第1章
text: Absolutely universal in the stories of all adults with ADD is the memory of never being comfortable about expressing their emotions.在所有患有注意力缺陷多动障碍的成年人的故事中，有一个共同点：他们始终觉得表达自己的情感是一件令人不自在的事情。

chapter: 第1章
text: The sensitive child, writes the Swiss psychotherapist Alice Miller, has “an amazing capacity to perceive and respond intuitively, that is unconsciously, to this need of the mother, or of both parents.”瑞士心理治疗师爱丽丝·米勒写道，那些敏感的孩子“具备一种惊人的能力——他们能够以直觉的方式，也就是在无意识的状态下，感知到母亲或父母双方的这种需求，并对此作出反应”。

chapter: 第1章
text: When they look inside themselves, they discover a frightening emptiness, a vacuum, an absence of a true self or of intrinsic motivation. Many a time I have heard ADD adults say, “I don’t know who I am,” or, “I don’t know what I want to do in my life.”当他们审视自己的内心时，会发现一种令人恐惧的空虚感——一种内在的真空状态，一种缺乏真正的自我或内在动力的感觉。我多次听到患有多动症的成年人说：“我不知道自己是谁”，或者“我不知道自己这一生想做什么”。

chapter: 第1章
text: It is ironic, but despite her poor impulse control, the ADD adult has persistently throttled her impulses, to use Henry Miller’s phrase. Submerged beneath a surface rippling with superficial and childish impulses are truer impulses for meaningful activity, the assertion of her autonomy, the pursuit of her own truth and human connectedness. The deeper these have sunk, the less one knows who she is or in which direction her path lies. Attaining self-esteem begins with finding our true impulses and raising them to the light of day.具有注意力缺陷多动障碍的成年人，尽管在控制自身冲动方面存在困难，但她们仍然一直在努力抑制自己的冲动——用亨利·米勒的话来说，就是一直在努力“抑制那些表面化、幼稚的冲动”。在这些表面冲动之下，隐藏着一些更为真实的冲动：追求有意义的活动、维护自己的自主性、探索属于自己的真理以及建立人与人之间的联系。然而，这些真正的冲动被压抑得越深，人们就越难以认清自己的本质，也越不知道自己应该走往何方。要建立起自尊，首先就必须找到自己真正的冲动，并将这些冲动带到光明的环境中来

chapter: 第1章
text: The episodes involving Elsa and David are implicit memories. Their emotional and physical reactions to witnessing the humiliation and rough handling of another human being are the reactivation of sensations first encoded during a much earlier time of their lives when they themselves were helpless and felt shame and humiliation.那些与艾莎和大卫有关的情节属于潜意识记忆。当他们目睹另一个人遭受羞辱与虐待时所表现出的情绪反应与身体反应，其实是对他们生命中早些时期所经历过的那些感受的重新激活——在那些时候，他们自己也曾经无助，也曾感受到羞耻与屈辱。There does not have to be severe trauma for neurological circuits to be encoded with emotions of exclusion, injustice and humiliation. It can happen in loving families, if a sensitive child has unconscious or even preverbal experiences of feeling alone and cut off, misunderstood and shamed.其实，并不需要遭受严重的创伤，神经回路才会被赋予“排斥、不公与羞辱”这些情感色彩。在充满爱的家庭中，如果一个敏感的孩子无意识地，甚至是在还不会说话的年纪，就经历了孤独、被孤立、被误解或被羞辱，这种情况也同样可能发生。

chapter: 第1章
text: The goal for the ADD adult is to move from the helplessness of identification to the empowered state of empathy.对于患有注意力缺陷多动障碍的成年人来说，他们的目标应该是从那种感到无助、无法自我帮助的状态，转变为能够具备同理心、能够自主应对各种情况的状态。

chapter: 第1章
text: Around authority figures such as employers, doctors, teachers and policemen, the ADD adult will experience a nervousness and lack of confidence that cannot be explained by the actual power relationship that exists in the present.在面对雇主、医生、教师或警察等权威人物时，患有注意力缺陷障碍的成年人会感到紧张且缺乏自信，而这种情绪无法用当前实际存在的权力关系来解释。

chapter: 第1章
text: One is again a child, facing powerful adults. “Like a child” is precisely how many ADD adults describe their sense of themselves in relationship to authority.其中一些人依然只是孩子，面对着那些拥有权力的成年人。“就像一个孩子”——正是许多患有多动症的成年人用来描述自己与权威人士之间的关系时的感受。

chapter: 第1章
text: The fear of intimacy is also a fear of the loss of self. There is the well-known paradox that the person with ADD craves real human contact, feels like an outsider and wishes to belong—but at the same time is reclusive, often preferring his own company to that of others.对亲密关系的恐惧，其实也意味着对自我认同感的丧失的恐惧。有一个众所周知的悖论：患有注意力缺陷障碍的人渴望与他人建立真实的人际联系，觉得自己像个局外人，希望融入群体之中；但与此同时，他们又往往倾向于独来独往，更喜欢独处，而不是与他人在一起。

chapter: 第1章
text: Developing a new view toward oneself is no easy task, for it goes against the grain of a lifetime of conditioning. It is not a matter of so-called positive thinking or the naive affirmations exemplified by vows like “Today I will be kinder to myself.” It requires the shedding, gradually, of defenses constructed long ago out of sheer necessity, defenses maintained out of the anxieties embedded in implicit memory.树立一种新的自我认知方式绝非易事，因为这与一个人一生中形成的各种思维模式背道而驰。这并非所谓的“积极思考”，也不仅仅是那些诸如“今天我要对自己更友善一些”之类的简单宣言所能实现的。事实上，这需要人们逐渐抛弃那些很久以前出于生存需要而形成的防御机制——那些因潜意识中的焦虑而长期被维持下来的防御机制。

text: The irony is that the energy ADD adults expend on their attempts at sameness is wasted, as is the anxiety parents generate over their child’s differentness. The world is much more ready to accept someone who is different and comfortable with it than someone desperately seeking to conform by denying himself. It’s the self-rejection others react against, much more than the differentness. So the solution for the adult is not to “fit in,” but to accept his inability to conform.具有注意力缺陷多动障碍的成年人为了追求“与众相同”而耗费的大量精力，其实都是白费了；而父母们因为孩子与众不同而产生的焦虑，也同样毫无意义。这个世界其实更愿意接受那些能够接受自己与众不同之处、并且对此感到坦然的人，而不是那些拼命拒绝自我、试图迎合他人的人。他人真正反感的，其实是这种自我否定，而非一个人与众不同的特质本身。因此，对于这些成年人来说，真正的解决办法并不是努力“融入群体”，而是接受自己无法遵从他人标准的这一事实。

text: 那些被内化的“不良对象”，其实是我们无法接受其负面特性的结果。我们试图在现实世界中远离它们，却又无法真正放弃或置之不理；在现实世界中我们无法掌控它们，因此便不断在内心努力占有它们、改变它们，迫使它们在我们的内在心理世界中变成“良性对象”。但它们永远都不会改变。

book: Schizoid Phenomena, Object-Relations and the Self
chapter: (a) Need of the Object and of Internal Object Relations
text: 只有当这种关系因对象的变化或死亡等原因而转变为“不良对象关系”时，对象才会以更彻底的方式被内化。当我们所需要和爱的人不再爱我们，或者其行为让我们觉得其不再充满爱意，又或者这个人消失了、去世了，也就是抛弃了我们，那么从情感和力比多的角度来看，这个人就变成了“不良对象”。这种情况可能发生在孩子身上：比如母亲拒绝给孩子喂奶、提前断奶，或者表现得愤怒、不耐烦且具有惩罚性；又或者因为疾病暂时或长期不在身边，甚至永远离开人世。同样，当我们所需要的人在情感上冷漠、疏离且不回应我们时，也会出现这种情况。这一切都被体验为最基本需求的挫败、被拒绝与抛弃，或是遭受迫害与攻击。此时，那个曾经的重要对象——如今已沦为“坏对象”——会在心理层面以比记忆更为深刻、更为根本的方式被内化。

关于自我反思的研究表明，当人们分析消极的自传体经历时，他们往往会采用一种沉浸式的视角，通过自己的眼睛重新想象那些经历的再现（Ayduk & Kross, 2010b; Grossmann & Kross, 2010; Verduyn, Van Mechelen, Kross, Chezzi, & Van Bever, 2012）。从这种视角来看，经历事件的“自我”与对事件进行思考的“自我”是同一个。不过，人们也有可能以一种自我疏离的视角来反思自己的经历，即从远处观察自己身处事件中的情形。在这种视角下，对事件进行思考的“自我”在心理上是与事件分离的。

chapter: Chapter 1
text: After so many years, I’ve learned that being creative is a full-time job with its own daily patterns. That’s why writers, for example, like to establish routines for themselves. The most productive ones get started early in the morning, when the world is quiet, the phones aren’t ringing, and their minds are rested, alert, and not yet polluted by other people’s words. They might set a goal for themselves—write fifteen hundred words, or stay at their desk until noon—but the real secret is that they do this every day. In other words, they are disciplined. Over time, as the daily routines become second nature, discipline morphs into habit.经过这么多年，我明白了，创意工作是一项全职工作，有自己的日常规律。这就是为什么作家们喜欢为自己建立日常规律。最有成效的作家们会在清晨开始工作，那时世界是安静的，电话不会响起，他们的头脑得到了休息，变得警觉，还没有被其他人的言语所污染。他们可能会为自己设定一个目标——写一千五百字，或者一直工作到中午——但真正的秘诀是，他们每天都会这样做。换句话说，他们很有纪律性。随着时间的推移，日常规律变成了第二天性，纪律也变成了习惯。

chapter: Chapter 1

It’s not only how we express what we remember, it’s how we interpret it—for ourselves and others.创造力更多的是关于提取我们存储的事实、虚构和情感，并找到新的方式来连接它们。我们在这里谈论的是隐喻。隐喻是一切艺术的生命力，如果不是艺术本身的话。隐喻是我们将现在所经历的事情与以前所经历的事情联系起来的词汇。它不仅是我们表达记忆的方式，也是我们为自己和他人诠释记忆的方式。

chapter: III. - THE SLOW HUNCH
text: Darwin’s notebooks lie at the tail end of a long and fruitful tradition that peaked in Enlightenment-era Europe, particularly in England: the practice of maintaining a “commonplace” book. Scholars, amateur scientists, aspiring men of letters—just about anyone with intellectual ambition in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries was likely to keep a commonplace book. The great minds of the period—Milton, Bacon, Locke—were zealous believers in the memory-enhancing powers of the commonplace book. In its most customary form, “commonplacing,” as it was called, involved transcribing interesting or inspirational passages from one’s reading, assembling a personalized encyclopedia of quotations. There is a distinct self-help quality to the early descriptions of commonplacing’s virtues: maintaining the books enabled one to “lay up a fund of knowledge, from which we may at all times select what is useful in the several pursuits of life.”达尔文的笔记是延续了启蒙运动时期欧洲，尤其是英国，一个漫长而富有成果的传统：保持“摘记”的习惯。学者、业余科学家、有抱负的文人——17、18世纪几乎所有有知识抱负的人，都有可能保持摘记的习惯。那个时代的大思想家——弥尔顿、培根、洛克——都是摘记这种习惯的狂热信徒。摘记最常见的形式是抄录阅读中有趣或有启发性的内容，汇编一本个性化的引语百科全书。摘记的早期描述中带有一种明显的自助色彩：保持摘记能让一个人“积累知识，从这些知识中，我们可以随时选取对生活的各个方面有用的内容”。

chapter: 前言 - Foreword
text: Writing is the simplest, most durable and enduring information recording system ever invented. When something is written on a durable medium, whether rock, marble, papyrus, leather or vellum, it endures indefinitely. To this day, we have samples of writing that come from the dawn of human civilization. Unlike information stored in a hard drive, something that is written down on a physical medium doesn’t crash, get erased or accidentally deleted. It doesn’t need any equipment or other technology to access and read. You simply open the medium it’s written on and read.写作是人类发明的最简单、最持久、最耐用的信息记录系统。当某种内容被记录在耐用的介质上，无论是岩石、大理石、纸莎草、皮革还是羊皮纸，它便能永久保存。直至今日，我们仍拥有源自人类文明黎明时期的文字样本。与存储在硬盘中的信息不同，记录在物理介质上的内容不会崩溃、被擦除或意外删除。它不需要任何设备或其他技术即可访问和阅读。你只需打开记录它的介质，然后阅读即可。

chapter: Introduction
text: A healing environment can provide critical support, but the gut-level change, the transformation from sorrow to acceptance to gratitude, can only come from deep within.

chapter: Introduction
text: 一个充满关爱的环境固然能提供重要的支持，但从内心深处产生真正的改变——从悲伤到接受，再到感恩——却需要依靠自己。

chapter: Introduction
text: Only when we go deep into the “forest”—the place deep within where we learn to rely upon ourselves and, through work and creation, allow our true selves to emerge—are we able to become whole and to heal.

chapter: Introduction
text: 只有当我们深入到那片‘森林’——内心深处那个让我们学会依靠自己的地方，在那里通过努力与创造让真实的自我得以显现——我们才能变得完整，并实现自我疗愈。

chapter: Introduction
text: There is now extensive research that shows writing—the simple act of putting down your deepest thoughts and feelings on paper—is one of the most powerful and effective means to ease and ultimately heal sorrow. The act of writing brings a structure and order to the chaos of grief. It taps into the healing power of your own unconscious. By giving voice to fears, anger, and despair, by letting go of old dreams and hopes, our self-healing powers come into play. The soul knows what it needs to heal. Through writing, it will lead you where you need to go.如今已有大量研究表明，写作——即将内心最深处的想法和感受记录在纸上的这一简单行为——是缓解悲伤、最终治愈伤痛的最有力、最有效的手段之一。写作为混乱的情绪带来了秩序与结构，它激发了人类潜意识中的治愈力量。通过表达恐惧、愤怒与绝望，放下旧有的梦想与期望，我们的自我治愈能力便得以发挥作用。灵魂本身知道自己需要什么来获得治愈；而写作会引导你走向正确的方向。

chapter: Introduction
text: The journey allows different routes to the destination. There are no wrong turns.

chapter: Introduction

chapter: Introduction
text: Write for yourself only, not for an audience.只为自己写作，而不是为读者写作。

chapter: Introduction
text: Where do I begin? How do I describe a process that is so personal, so intimate, so haphazard? How do I describe the need I had to sit in silence, open my notebook, and begin day after day, not knowing what might appear? How do I describe the initial trepidation, the times of quiet when no words came, the hours when words flowed like a rushing river that nothing could keep within its banks? How do I let people know that only through writing was I able to let go of my dreams for Katherine and love her as she is, and my life as it is? How do I describe the mysterious alchemy that transmutes our personal grief, anger, and incomprehension into a spaciousness of heart and mind?我该从哪里开始呢？该如何描述这样一个如此个人化、如此私密、又如此充满偶然性的过程呢？该如何表达我那种渴望静静地坐下来，打开笔记本，日复一日地写下去的冲动——尽管我根本不知道接下来会写出什么来呢？该如何描述最初的忐忑不安、那些无言以对的时刻，以及那些文字如奔腾的河流般汹涌而出、无法被任何东西阻挡住的时光呢？我又该如何让人们明白：只有通过写作，我才能放下对凯瑟琳的那些幻想，接受她真实的模样，也接受自己真实的生活呢？又该如何描述那种神奇的“炼金术”呢？它将我们内心的悲伤、愤怒与困惑转化为一种心灵与思想的宽广与宁静呢？

chapter: Chapter 1 - Going Through Pain
text: Crises hit like avalanches. Everything is going fine. Then all of a sudden, the earth shifts. It can be a cancer diagnosis, a car accident, the complications of childbirth, the death of a friend, the arrest of a child, the loss of a job, the end of a marriage. Dreams shatter, and we fear the pieces of our lives can never be glued together again. We cry out, but no one can hear us. We fall deeper into darkness and have no idea if we’ll ever see light again.危机如雪崩般突然降临。一切原本都进行得很顺利，然而转眼间，一切都变了。这可能是癌症的诊断结果，也可能是车祸、分娩时的并发症、朋友的离世、孩子的被捕、失业，或是婚姻的终结。我们的梦想破碎了，我们害怕生活的碎片再也无法重新拼凑起来。我们大声呼喊，却无人能听见；我们陷入更深的黑暗中，不知道自己是否还能重见光明。

chapter: Chapter 1 - Going Through Pain
text: Yet we need to understand that what is functional at one point may be dysfunctional at another. After the initial shock, we have to move from surviving to thriving. That can only be done when we acknowledge, and ultimately embrace, the full extent of the loss; when we go through our grief. If we don’t, we die, or something in us dies.然而，我们需要明白：在某个阶段看似有效的方法，在另一个阶段可能会变得无效。在最初的震惊过后，我们必须从仅仅“生存”转变为“蓬勃发展”。只有当我们承认并最终接受这一切损失时，才能实现这一转变；只有当我们经历自己的悲伤过程时，才能真正做到这一点。如果我们不这样做，要么我们自己会“死去”，要么我们内心的某些东西也会“死去”。

chapter: Chapter 1 - Going Through Pain
text: I realize now that part of going through grief involves entering fully into the tragedy, acknowledging the enormity of what has happened, and understanding that something profound has been taken away forever.

chapter: Chapter 1 - Going Through Pain
text: 现在我明白了，经历悲伤的过程意味着要完全沉浸在悲剧之中，承认所发生事情的严重性，并接受某些重要东西已经永远离我们而去的事实。

chapter: Chapter 2 - Expectations Revisited
text: We are miserable, at some level convinced we brought our misfortunes upon ourselves. Fear of the future paralyzes us with anxiety. How will we cope? How will we make it through this disaster?

chapter: Chapter 2 - Expectations Revisited
text: 我们生活在痛苦之中，内心深处坚信自己的不幸都是自己造成的。对未来的恐惧让我们陷入焦虑之中，无法动弹。我们该如何应对这一切？又该如何熬过这场灾难呢？

chapter: Chapter 2 - Expectations Revisited
text: At the same time, we have a vision of what our lives were supposed to be. This, definitely, is not it. We have experienced a series of little deaths as our expectations crumbled. It is essential that we mourn the loss of those expectations, which shaped our mind-sets and created our personal worldviews.与此同时，我们对自己的生活原本应该是什么样子有着某种设想。但现实显然并非如此。当我们的期望逐渐破灭时，我们经历了一系列“精神上的死亡”（即心理上的打击）。我们必须为这些期望的失落而哀悼，因为这些期望曾塑造我们的思维方式，也构成了我们的个人世界观。

chapter: Chapter 3 - Trying to Fix It
text: Writing is the most profound way of codifying your thoughts, the best way of learning from yourself who you are and what you believe.写作是将你的思想以文字形式记录下来的最深刻的方式，也是了解自己、认识自己的信念的最佳途径。—WARREN BENNIS, On Becoming a Leader——沃伦·本尼斯，《如何成为领导者》

chapter: Chapter 4 - Learning from Others
text: When we start writing our stories, we begin to discover aspects of our lives that we didn’t know existed. Through this process of unearthing, of digging beneath the surface layer to something richer and darker, we find the gems within.

chapter: Chapter 4 - Learning from Others
text: 当我们开始书写自己的故事时，我们便开始发现生活中一些此前未曾察觉的存在。通过这个挖掘的过程——从表面之下探寻更深层次、更丰富、更复杂的内容——我们发现了那些隐藏其中的“珍宝”。

chapter: Chapter 5 - Experiencing Death
text: There is power in contemplating death. By doing so, we think more about how we should live our lives. We focus more on what is important to us right now. We are forced to live more in the present, reminded of the preciousness of each moment. We open our hearts as we realize that we all are literally in the same boat, headed in the same direction. Thinking about death helps clear away the cobwebs of complacency and entitlement. It moves us closer to compassion for others and for ourselves.思考死亡本身蕴含着一种力量。通过这样的思考，我们会更加反思自己应该如何生活，更加关注当下对我们来说真正重要的事情。这迫使我们更加活在当下，让我们意识到每一刻的珍贵。当我们意识到所有人其实都处于同样的处境、朝着同一个方向前进时，我们的心也会变得更加敞开。思考死亡有助于消除自满与特权意识带来的消极情绪，让我们更加懂得去关爱他人和自己。

chapter: Chapter 5 - Experiencing Death
text: Write about death. Focusing on death is not a macabre exercise, but a tool for enhancing your life right now.
